documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call. Discharged 12/30 after 7 days of IV ceftriaxone for disseminated gonococcal infection. Home, no fevers, walking fine, knee and wrist better each day. No discharge meds to reconcile, takes nothing at home. Confirmed appointment Thursday 1/4 at 11. Knows to call for fever or a hot, swollen joint.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 5 days after discharge. Admitted 12/24-12/30 for disseminated gonococcal infection: fever, right knee and left wrist arthritis, left hand flexor tenosynovitis, pustular rash, cervicitis. Cervical NAAT positive for GC, CT negative. Blood and knee fluid cultures negative. 7 days of IV ceftriaxone completed inpatient. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Since home: no fevers. Knee and wrist much better, still a little stiff in the mornings. Spots on the arms and ankles scabbing over. No discharge or spotting now. Hasn't been sexually active since. Has told recent partners to get tested.

Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals normal. Right knee with mild residual swelling, no warmth, flexes nearly fully. Left wrist mildly puffy, near-full range of motion, grip ok. Flexor tendons of the left hand not tender. Skin: crusted, fading lesions on the forearms and ankles.

A/P:
1. DGI, improving after a full course of ceftriaxone. CBC and CRP today to make sure they're trending down. Recheck in 2-3 weeks.
2. Retest GC/CT around late March.
3. Condoms every time going forward; we talked about partner testing and how she'd know if it came back.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: White count is back to normal (6.8) and the inflammation marker CRP is down to 6 from 96 in the ED. Good recovery. See you on the 22nd.

documents.title: Gynecology Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGY OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 12/19/2024
Copy to primary care.

CC: three days of fever, malaise, painful urination and worsening genital pain.

HPI: 27 y/o seen here previously for condylomata, with a disseminated gonococcal infection last December. Three days of feeling feverish and achy with chills, burning on urination, and genital tenderness that keeps increasing; sitting is difficult because of vulvar pain. No abnormal discharge and no pelvic pain.

Problem list: condylomata acuminata; molluscum contagiosum; disseminated gonococcal infection (treated 12/2023).
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother hypothyroidism; father hypertension; sibling healthy.
SH: three male partners in the last six months. Condoms inconsistently. No contraception.

Vitals: T 37.0 C, P 80, BP 110/70.

Pelvic exam: multiple vesicles and shallow ulcers over the labia minora and majora, exquisitely tender to light touch. Bilateral inguinal lymph nodes enlarged, firm and tender.

Assessment: primary genital herpes simplex infection.

Plan:
- Lesion swab for HSV PCR; GC/CT NAAT.
- Valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 10 days.
- Sitz baths; urinating in a warm bath or with a peri bottle helps the burning.
- Abstain until lesions are fully healed.

Addendum 12/21: PCR positive for HSV-2, negative for HSV-1. GC/CT negative. Patient informed by phone; discussed lifelong latency, possible recurrences, asymptomatic shedding and disclosure to partners.

documents.body: Just wanted to say I'm a lot better. Fever gone after a couple days and the sores are healing. Gyn told me it's HSV-2. Kind of devastated honestly. Can we talk about it sometime?

documents.title: RE: update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Really glad you're feeling better. Yes, of course. It's very common and very manageable, and I'm happy to go through it with you. I put you on for a video visit Monday 1/6 at 4.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, patient at home.

First-episode genital herpes diagnosed by gyn 12/19, PCR HSV-2. Finished 10 days of valacyclovir. Sores healed, no fever, urinating comfortably.

Mostly wanted to talk. Covered: HSV-2 stays in the body and may or may not recur, first episodes are usually the worst; it can be passed on without symptoms; condoms lower risk; telling partners before sex. Answered her questions about dating. She seemed relieved.

A/P: Primary genital HSV-2, episode resolved. Message at the first tingling or sores so we can arrange to be seen. Annual physical in September.

documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Gynecology office visit, 01/05/2026. cc: PCP.

Reason for visit: painful genital sores and burning with urination for 4 days.

History: 28 year old with prior condylomata, DGI (2023), and a primary genital herpes episode in December 2024 (HSV-2 by PCR). This started with genital burning and tingling, then small fluid-filled blisters that opened into shallow, tender sores. Low-grade fevers, fatigue, sore lumps in the groin.

Problems: condylomata acuminata; molluscum contagiosum; disseminated gonococcal infection; genital herpes.
Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: one new partner; condoms not consistently.

Exam: multiple shallow, red, clean-based ulcers on the vulva and outer labia. Bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Assessment: recurrent genital herpes.

Plan: swab of one ulcer for HSV PCR. Valacyclovir 1 g daily for 5 days. Comfort measures as before. Avoid sexual contact until healed and let her partner know.

Addendum 01/07: PCR positive for HSV-2.

Gynecology
